AnimatedTitle.description: A large title with an optional subtitle and an animated underline. Good for intros and transitions.
AnimatedTitle.useWhen: scene 0 hook or final outro — a dramatic title with stakes

ComparisonCard.description: A card displaying a side-by-side comparison with pros and cons. Good for evaluating options.
ComparisonCard.useWhen: head-to-head pros vs cons of one subject

BulletList.description: A bulleted or numbered list with staggered reveal animation.
BulletList.useWhen: 5-7 specific claims, each with a number or system name

StepFlow.description: A horizontal step-by-step flow diagram with an animated connector line.
StepFlow.useWhen: 4-6 sequential steps, each starting with an action verb

StatCallout.description: A large statistic callout with an animated counting number.

ArchitectureDiagram.description: Renders an architecture diagram with servers, databases, and load balancers connected by animated data streams and arrows. Specify nodes and connections.
ArchitectureDiagram.useWhen: system topology with servers, DBs, load balancers

SplitScreen.description: A layout scene showing a title, bullet points, code snippets, and optional media on the right side. Great for explaining technical concepts.
SplitScreen.useWhen: text bullets and a code snippet together

TypewriterText.description: Animated typewriter effect with a blinking cursor. Reveals one or more lines of text character by character. Great for code reveals or dramatic text.

TimelineFlow.description: An animated vertical or horizontal timeline with events appearing in staggered sequence. Use for history, roadmaps, or step-by-step processes.
TimelineFlow.useWhen: chronological history with real dates and events

QuoteCard.description: A full-screen animated pull quote with an optional highlight sweep on key words and author attribution. Great for testimonials and impactful statements.
QuoteCard.useWhen: a real verbatim quote from a paper, talk, or engineer

CodeBlock.description: A macOS-style code window with syntax highlighting, line numbers, and optional line-by-line reveal animation. Ideal for showing code examples.

TwoColumnLayout.description: A two-column comparison layout with an animated center divider. Each column has a heading and bullet points that slide in from opposite sides.
TwoColumnLayout.useWhen: parallel comparison of two subjects (before/after, X vs Y)

BarChart.description: An animated bar chart with vertical or horizontal layout. Bars grow in with spring physics and values count up from 0. Use for data comparisons.

PacketFlow.description: An animated network topology where data packets travel along edges between nodes. Nodes are positioned by x/y percentage coordinates. Ideal for showing network protocols, request routing, TCP handshakes, and distributed system data flows.
PacketFlow.useWhen: data packets traveling a network (protocols, routing)

HttpExchange.description: A side-by-side HTTP request and response viewer with line-by-line animated reveal. Shows method, path, headers, and body for both request and response. Great for explaining APIs, REST calls, and HTTP protocol details.
HttpExchange.useWhen: an HTTP request/response pair (REST, API, protocol)

HashRing.description: A consistent hashing ring with virtual nodes, server placement, and animated key lookups. Use for distributed caches, sharded databases, CDNs, and any consistent-hashing explanation.

StateMachine.description: An animated finite-state machine with state boxes, labeled transition arrows, and a pulsing active state. Use for protocol diagrams (TCP handshake, Raft consensus), cache coherence, and workflow states.

TreeHierarchy.description: A top-down tree diagram with auto-laid-out nodes and curved connectors. Use for B-trees, DNS hierarchy, recursion trees, file systems, org charts, and classification.
TreeHierarchy.useWhen: hierarchical structure (B-tree, DNS, file system, org)

SequenceDiagram.description: A UML-style sequence diagram with actor lifelines and time-ordered request/response arrows. Use for API flows, microservice communication, and authentication sequences.

LineChart.description: An animated multi-series line chart with optional area fill, grid lines, and legend. Lines draw in over time. Use for trends, growth curves, latency vs load, and any time-series comparison.
LineChart.useWhen: trends over time, growth curves, latency vs load

MathFormula.description: A centered formula display with token-based rendering for variables, numbers, fractions, exponents, subscripts, square roots, and sums. Use for Big-O notation, equations, and math derivations.
MathFormula.useWhen: a single key equation or Big-O expression

EquationDerivation.description: A vertical stack of formula steps connected by arrows, with optional justifications. Each step is a complete formula that can highlight independently. Use for proof walks and algebraic transformations.
EquationDerivation.useWhen: a multi-step proof or algebraic derivation

TerminalCLI.description: An animated terminal/CLI window that types a command then streams output line by line. Themes: dark, matrix, amber. Use for tutorials, debugging flows, and showing command output.
TerminalCLI.useWhen: a command plus its streamed terminal output

PieChart.description: An animated pie or donut chart with a sweeping reveal, percentage labels, an optional center label, and a side legend with values. Use for proportional breakdowns.

NumberedList.description: A list of numbered cards with large colored badges, headings, and descriptions. Stack (vertical) or grid (2-column) layout. Use for ranked steps, principles, and ordered concepts.
NumberedList.useWhen: ranked principles or ordered top-N items

GlossaryCards.description: A grid of term/definition cards with colored icon tiles. Auto-detects 2- or 3-column layout. Use for vocabulary sections, acronym glossaries, and concept maps.
GlossaryCards.useWhen: vocabulary, acronym glossary, or concept map

FlowDiagram.description: A branching flow diagram with process (rectangle), decision (diamond), and start/end (pill) shapes connected by labeled arrows. Use for workflows, conditional logic, and algorithms with branching.

CalloutAnnotation.description: A highlighted callout box with corner brackets, a side arrow, and optional bullet points. Use to emphasize a key insight or definition against a darker background.
CalloutAnnotation.useWhen: emphasize a key insight or definition in prose

SortingVisualizer.description: An animated sorting-algorithm walkthrough. Bars represent values; steps compare, swap, partition, set, or merge-write to visualise bubble / merge / quick / heap / radix / counting sort.
SortingVisualizer.useWhen: a sorting algorithm being walked through, or comparing sort algorithms visually

LinearStructure.description: An animated linear data structure — array, stack, queue, deque, or linked list — with push/pop/enqueue/dequeue/insert/delete motion. Cells shift, fade, and translate to visualise each operation.
LinearStructure.useWhen: a linear data structure — array, stack, queue, deque, or linked list — being mutated by a sequence of operations

ArrayAlgorithm.description: An animated array walkthrough with pointer overlays. Modes: binary-search (L/M/R), sliding-window (start/end + running sum), two-pointer (i/j).
ArrayAlgorithm.useWhen: an array-scan algorithm — binary search, sliding window, or two-pointer technique

DPTableVisualizer.description: An animated 2D DP table. Cells fill in order with dependency arrows from prior cells; optional final path traces the optimal answer.
DPTableVisualizer.useWhen: a 2D DP table being filled cell-by-cell, or a matrix-based algorithm (LCS, edit distance, Floyd-Warshall, knapsack)

GraphTraversal.description: An animated graph algorithm walkthrough. Node states (unvisited/frontier/visited/settled) and edge states (traversed/relaxed/MST/rejected) update per step. Supports DFS, BFS, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, topological sort, Prim's and Kruskal's MST.
GraphTraversal.useWhen: a graph algorithm being traced — DFS/BFS traversal, shortest path (Dijkstra/Bellman-Ford), MST, or topological sort

RecursionTree.description: An animated recursion tree. Nodes grow in DFS order, then unwind with return values. Supports backtracking pruning (red dead-ends, green success paths) and memoization (memo-hit nodes stay collapsed).
RecursionTree.useWhen: a recursive call tree, backtracking search, or memoization pattern being walked through
